credits_cram.why: CRAM is called an existing framework with an 'independent re-implementation', but Hoover, Blayney and Whittington are never named or credited.

cites_hoover.why: The only citations are Bai2019, Salvatori2026, Valmeekam2023 and Kong2026; none is the CRAM paper.

small_n.why: 'direct solving is evaluated on... 5 puzzles each for Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5, and 10 puzzles for Haiku 5.5', with a stated small-sample caveat.

handset_caveat.why: 'unlearned hand-set energy baseline... solves 497 out of 500', matching learned CRAM at 496-497.

their_numbers.why: The 42 ms H200 fit time is attributed to 'prior literature' and the 99.996% to what CRAM 'reports'; our own timings are given separately.

no_new_claims.why: It adds unlogged details: Python 3.11, all 9 solvers using MRV, solvers solving the CRAM-failed puzzles in under 2 ms, and a '5 orders of magnitude' speedup claim.
